issue.body:
The Angular JIT compiler uses the output of TypeScript's `emitDecoratorMetadata` to support dependency injection at runtime.  This option stores type and DI token information so that the runtime JIT compiler can inject the proper provider.  This option is not needed for AOT compilation and the metadata is indirectly stripped from the output due to all Angular decorators being removed during the compilation process.

Unfortunately, the `emitDecoratorMetadata` option does not support forward references (or more generally circular dependencies) within ES2015+ output due to the TypeScript compiler transforming the metadata into a direct reference of the yet to be defined class.  This results in a runtime TDZ error.  This is a known limitation of the `emitDecoratorMetadata` option ([reference](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/27519)).  This situation is not unique to Angular and can occur in any TypeScript code.  As it is marked as a design limitation, it is considered that it cannot be fixed within the current architecture of TypeScript.

As a result, the change in this PR removes the need for the use of the option by storing the DI information in a static property function via the use of the tsickle `ctorParameters` transformation.  By leveraging the existing functionality, no changes to the framework code is necessary.  Also, minimal new code is required within the CLI, as the relevant tsickle code can be extracted and used with several local modifications.

For forward references to function in ES2015+, the `emitDecoratorMetadata` option must be disabled based on the current implementation.  To support both the option and forward references, the metadata generated by TypeScript would need to be altered to remove the type information that would trigger a TDZ error.  However, by doing so the metadata information is no longer useful to Angular and technically incorrect as it will not contain the information from the source code as described by the option.

Closes: #14424

body:
Just an addition to this, I remember that @alexeagle & @vikerman had a discussion with the Google TypeScript team and it was brought up that outside of Google unless using Closure there shouldn't be the need for tsickle. However seeing the latest issues, the above and https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/14473 maybe it is. 

Tsickle will be re-introduced when generating libraries with CLI, however of course users might still opt-out if they want to use `resolveJsonModule` for example see https://github.com/angular/tsickle/pull/922. the main reason for this not to go in was not to increase the scope of tsickle.

This issue is mostly about projects *not* using the CLI but depending on libraries which no longer aren't transformed by `tsickle`. Tsickle previously was part of the default workflow with `ngc` and now it no longer is enabled by default.

The components repository still opts-in for `tsickle` decorator downleveling but we aren't able to do this when switching to Bazel (as mentioned in the issue description).

To be clear: Yes. In my opinion `tsickle` always did more than just making output closure-compatible. It had the nice side-effect of decorator downleveling for Angular / and making it SSR compatible.

History: when we first needed decorator downleveling around Angular 2 timeframe, TS didn't have CustomTransformers. tsickle was the closest thing available so we added the functionality there.

Now, it doesn't make sense. tsickle should be "ts to closure" (that's where the name derives: ts2cl) and the decorator downleveling should be a transpile step for all Angular code. I wish it was baked right into tsc/ngc using CustomTransformer but I guess putting it in the webpack layer via angular/angular-cli#14473 is our short-term answer to keep forwardRef working in target=es2015

Totally agreed that `tsickle` should be `TypeScript to Closure` only. Also agreed that ideally the decorator downleveling would be part of NGC.. Similarly to how `ngtsc` already handles the decorator downleveling. 

I'm not sure if it's worth doing anything to make it work for non-CLI applications in the meanwhile since we still have the `opt-in` for tsickle right now (which could stay until ngtsc is the default AFAIK). Though what we miss right now is a temporary solution to make this work with Bazel. There is no way to only opt into the decorator downleveling from `tsickle`.

The `design:type` metadata is a result of the TS `emitDecoratorMetadata` option, which is only needed in JIT to support dependency injection and is separate from decorator downleveling/removal.  If JIT mode is not required then the TS option can be removed. ([relevant TS code](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/transformers/ts.ts#L1668))

Regardless, the custom transformer introduced in `@ngtools/webpack` for 8.0 should ideally be moved into ngc proper (with additional refactoring and cleanup -- the code was intended to minimize risk by leveraging the existing Tsickle code as much as possible).  However, the transformer would also need to be present in the CLI as the Angular compiler is not used in JIT mode.

Also of interest is that TypeScript has an alternative format for the metadata that uses arrow functions.  However, it is disabled via a hardcoded constant. https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/master/src/compiler/transformers/ts.ts#L1659

> The `design:type` metadata is a result of the TS `emitDecoratorMetadata` option, which is only needed in JIT to support dependency injection and is separate from decorator downleveling/removal. If JIT mode is not required then the TS option can be removed.

@clydin Even some transformer rewrites the parameter type to a value production, TypeScript will still remove its import, resulting in broken code, which happens in https://github.com/angular/tsickle/issues/635.

The root cause of this issue is the use of the TypeScript `emitDecoratorMetadata` option.  Tsickle is only relevant here because it removes the decorators.  This effectively disables the option as there is no "decorator metadata" to emit without the decorators.  Further, no transform of the parameter types is necessary outside of providing JIT mode support.  As such, if JIT mode support is not required then this problem is effectively void.

issue.body:
We want to enable tsickle for decorator processing. This was one of the
blockers for using the bazel packages in releases as unprocessed decorators
will end up referencing DOM specific globals (e.g. `HTMLElement`).

These references would then break server-side rendering for non CLI
projects. Read more about this https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/30586
